items.title: Remove the fixed-length truncation so late-diverging rejection reasons keep distinct digests
items.context: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:479 truncates the normalized reason to 200 characters before hashing. ProofStory gap lists share a preamble longer than that, so two different gaps hash identically. Hash the full normalized reason, retaining only a large sanity bound to cap CPU on pathological input.
items.userSees: node packages/main/dist/tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.js prints a passing check stating that two real DEV-gate rejection renders differing only past the former 200-character cut produce different digest keys.

happy.desc: gateFailureDigest applied to two reconstructions of the real DEV-gate rejection render (machine.ts:179 preamble plus renderProofStoryDiagnosticReport), identical for their first 244 normalized characters and differing only in the outstanding gap codes, returns two different keys.
The same two rejections routed through bumpGateFailureCount leave maxGateFailureCount at 1, so assessBreaker does not trip, which is the actual operator-visible consequence.

edge.desc: A rejection reason far longer than any realistic gate message still produces a digest, and the retained sanity bound is exercised rather than silently absent.
Two reasons that are identical up to the sanity bound and differ only beyond it are documented as collapsing, so the bound's residual behavior is stated rather than assumed away.

adversarial.desc: Restoring only the fixed-length truncation makes the new smoke assertions fail, proving the check is bound to this change and not to some unrelated property.

verificationEvidence.note: NOT DELIVERED BY THIS STORY, and recorded as such rather than claimed. The C1 class this intent targets was fixed on main by story B-cc54 (v0.3.231), which keeps the 200-character prefix and folds structurally-extracted gap-id signals into the hash basis. This branch adopted main's version wholesale at merge commit 2d12079855 and changed neither the truncation nor the basis. Verified: the RED harness run against main's own build reports C1a and C1b PASSING, so the user-visible outcome is true on main today.

The same case drives the real bumpGateFailureCount for both rejections and reports counter=1 breaker=proceed, so the operator-visible consequence (no freeze) is asserted, not just the hash. 'dev-gate-gap-count-differs' proves the same where gap COUNTS differ.

Case 'must-still-collapse sanity-bound-is-applied [guard: sanity-bound]' asserts an oversize reason digests EXACTLY as its own bounded prefix. Deleting the bound fails exactly {beyond-sanity-bound, sanity-bound-is-applied} and leaves the other 28 passing, reproduced independently by the test-coverage lane. Replaces the F-012 citation of a shape-check that passed with or without the bound.

Case 'must-still-collapse beyond-sanity-bound [guard: sanity-bound]' asserts two reasons identical up to the bound and differing only past it still share one key, documenting the residual rather than assuming it away.

Revert-proof re-derived against the round-4 matrix: restoring the pre-story 200-character cut fails exactly {dev-gate-one-gap-differs, dev-gate-gap-count-differs} (guard truncation-removal) and leaves the other 28 passing.

items.title: Narrow the path normalizer to machine-specific absolute roots only
items.context: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:475 rewrites any slash-bearing token, collapsing DEV/REVIEW with DEV/TEST and src/core/alpha.ts with src/core/beta.ts. Restrict it to absolute paths anchored at machine-specific roots so relative repo paths and slash-bearing identifiers stay distinct while host-varying paths still collapse.
items.userSees: The convergence-breaker smoke prints passing checks stating that DEV/REVIEW and DEV/TEST digest differently, that two files under a shared first path segment digest differently, and that the same lock path under /Users and under /private/var still digests identically.

happy.desc: Two rejection reasons differing only in a slash-bearing identifier (the phase pair DEV/REVIEW versus DEV/TEST) produce different digest keys.
Two rejection reasons naming different repo-relative files under a shared first segment (src/core/alpha.ts versus src/core/beta.ts) produce different digest keys.

edge.desc: The same logical lock path rendered under a machine-specific root (/Users/... versus /private/var/...) still produces one digest key, so host-varying paths keep collapsing.
A path that begins at a machine-specific root but continues into repo-relative segments is normalized once, without leaving a partially-rewritten remainder that could differ per host.

adversarial.desc: Restoring the greedy slash-anchored regex makes the new distinctness checks fail while the machine-path collapse check keeps passing, proving both directions are independently bound to this change.

verificationEvidence.note: Case 'must-differ phase-pair [guard: path-rule-overreach]' asserts DEV/REVIEW and DEV/TEST give keys=2 counter=1 breaker=proceed. Tag split from the round-2 'path-rule' after cross-host codex showed one tag conflated two opposite dependencies.
Case 'must-differ in-repo-file-path [guard: path-rule-overreach]' asserts two files under a shared first segment give keys=2 counter=1 breaker=proceed.

Case 'must-still-collapse machine-absolute-path [guard: path-rule-collapse]' asserts the same logical lock path under /Users and under /private/var gives keys=1 counter=2 breaker=trips; 'delimiter-attached-absolute-path' extends it to paths introduced by a colon, equals or comma; 'windows-absolute-path' covers drive-letter paths.

Case 'must-still-collapse machine-path-into-repo-relative-segments [guard: path-rule-collapse]' asserts a path continuing from a machine root into repo-relative segments is consumed in one match, leaving no per-host remainder.

Two re-derived revert-proofs, one per direction: widening the path rule back to any-slash fails exactly {phase-pair, in-repo-file-path}; deleting the POSIX rule fails exactly the three path-rule-collapse cases; deleting the Windows rule fails only {windows-absolute-path}. Each leaves every other case passing.

items.title: Narrow the numeric normalizer to standalone numbers only
items.context: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:476 rewrites digit runs inside identifier tokens, collapsing CHK-001 with CHK-002. Restrict it so digits attached to an identifier survive while free-standing counters such as attempt numbers still collapse.
items.userSees: The convergence-breaker smoke prints a passing check stating that a rejection naming CHK-001 and one naming CHK-002 digest differently, alongside a passing check that two attempts differing only in a free-standing counter still digest identically.

happy.desc: Two rejection reasons differing only in an identifier-embedded ordinal (CHK-001 versus CHK-002) produce different digest keys.

edge.desc: Two rejection reasons differing only in free-standing counters and an ISO timestamp still produce one digest key, so genuine retries of one failure keep accumulating.
A story id such as B-bf52, whose digits are attached to an identifier, survives normalization, so rejections naming different stories are not conflated.

adversarial.desc: Restoring the unconditional digit-run rewrite makes the identifier-ordinal distinctness check fail while the free-standing-counter collapse check keeps passing.

verificationEvidence.note: Case 'must-differ checklist-ordinal [guard: digit-rule-overreach]' asserts CHK-001 and CHK-002 give keys=2 counter=1 and prints both compared values literally; 'review-round-ordinal', 'story-id' and 'dotted-version-requirement' extend the same direction.

HONEST DIVERGENCE FROM THE FROZEN userSees. This intent asks that two attempts differing only in a free-standing counter still collapse. Round 4 re-decided that direction: case 'must-differ attempt-counter-now-distinct [guard: number-rule-removal]' now asserts the OPPOSITE, and 'must-still-collapse iso-timestamp-only [guard: iso-timestamp-rule]' carries the surviving half (the timestamp still collapses with the ordinal held constant). Reason, recorded in plan.md: a bare number in free text is not syntactically decidable as substantive or volatile; the fixture shape "(attempt N)" has NO real producer anywhere in this repo, existing only as the smoke's own invented string; and the general rule was collapsing REAL substantive values, because test-evidence output is interpolated verbatim into a story_advance DONE rejection at machine.ts:1190, so "connection to localhost:3000 refused" and the same with port 4000 shared one counter key and two DIFFERENT validation failures would falsely freeze the story. Failing toward distinct fails toward never falsely freezing, which is this story's purpose; runaway retries are separately covered by the burn-alert system.

Case 'must-differ story-id [guard: digit-rule-overreach]' asserts a story id whose digits attach to an identifier survives normalization; 'must-differ identifier-attached-long-decimal [guard: attached-hash-overreach]' extends this to 7-or-more-digit suffixes, which the hex rule used to swallow (F-014), while 'must-still-collapse ppid-derived-session-id [guard: attached-hash-collapse]' proves the converse for a real ppid-derived sess-<hash> (F-022): an attached hex run is normalized only when it contains an a-f letter, which is provably a digest rather than an ordinal.

Re-derived revert-proofs: reintroducing the narrow number rule fails exactly the six number-rule-removal cases; reintroducing the unconditional digit rewrite fails those plus the four digit-rule-overreach cases plus identifier-attached-long-decimal; widening the attached-hash rule fails only {identifier-attached-long-decimal}; deleting it fails only {ppid-derived-session-id}. Both directions are independently bound.

items.title: Extend the convergence-breaker smoke with a substantive-versus-incidental digest matrix
items.context: packages/main/src/tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.ts:180-182 asserts distinct reasons do not accumulate but uses fixtures too short and too plain to reach any collapse rule. Add the four must-differ cases (long-preamble ProofStory gaps, phase pair, checklist ids, in-repo file paths) and the three must-still-collapse cases (timestamps and attempt counters, machine-specific absolute paths, hex digests), each driving the real bumpGateFailureCount and maxGateFailureCount path so the counter consequence is proven, not just the hash.
items.userSees: npm run test:convergence-breaker exits zero and its output lists the must-differ and must-still-collapse digest cases by name, each reporting the resulting gate-failure counter value rather than only the hash.

happy.desc: Every must-differ case drives the real bumpGateFailureCount path twice and then asserts maxGateFailureCount is 1, proving the counter consequence rather than only the hash inequality.
npm run test:convergence-breaker exits zero from a clean build, so the matrix is reachable through the root full test suite that gates DONE.

edge.desc: Every must-still-collapse case drives bumpGateFailureCount twice and asserts maxGateFailureCount reaches 2 and assessBreaker still trips, proving the breaker keeps catching a genuine repeat.
The pre-existing assertions in this smoke, including the reset-clears-counter case, keep passing unchanged alongside the new matrix.

adversarial.desc: Each of the three normalizer changes reverted individually causes a named subset of the matrix to fail and leaves the rest passing, so the matrix localizes which rule regressed instead of failing as one opaque block.

verificationEvidence.note: All 15 must-differ cases print 'keys=2 counter=1 breaker=proceed', each having driven the real bumpGateFailureCount twice and read back maxGateFailureCount and assessBreaker, so the counter consequence is proven rather than hash inequality alone. Count re-recorded for the round-4 matrix (was 9 in round 3).

Ran from a clean build in the worktree and exited zero, confirming the 30-case matrix is reachable through the root npm test chain (package.json:15 via :116) that lattice.config.json lists as a doneRequiredCommand.

All 15 must-still-collapse cases print 'keys=1 counter=2 breaker=trips', proving the breaker still catches a genuine repeat under the narrowed policy. They cover the four real lease/lock contention messages, sentence-final durations, a decimal duration straddling the hash threshold, a real ppid-derived session id, ISO timestamps alone, three machine-path shapes, Windows paths, free-standing hashes and both sanity-bound cases.

The smoke's PASS line still enumerates every pre-existing assertion alongside the matrix across four fix rounds, including gate-repeat digest/reset, no-spurious-reset, thresholds, autopilot refusal and F-003 takeover re-baseline.

Fourteen re-derived revert-proofs across ten guard groups, every guard tag re-derived from scratch after the round-4 policy change (none survived unchanged). The number-rule-removal group makes the policy decision itself revertible and therefore falsifiable: reintroducing the deleted rule fails exactly its six cases. Guard tags were split into overreach/collapse pairs for path, digit and hash precisely because single tags mis-localized -- cross-host codex caught the path and attached-decimal conflations, and the implementer caught two more (hex-id mis-tagged as digit-rule; two lock fixtures varying pid as well as age, now holding pid constant).
